source.title: Faster-GCG: Efficient Discrete Optimization Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiao Li; Wei Zhang; Zhuhong Li; Qiong-Xiu Li; Shei PernChua; Bingze Lee; Jinghao Cui; Yi-Fan Huang; Xiao-Lin Hu

record.tranche_reason: Reports harmful-output scores for adversarial suffix attacks, testing whether suffixes can bypass refusal, but does not test compliant-opening prefills, response-position KL, fine-tuning, or safety localization.
record.gate_note: The study tests adversarial suffix attacks and reports their harmfulness scores. It does not test fine-tuning, response-token KL concentration, or whether safety is localized in parameters. Reported ASRs are averages of normalized harmfulness scores from two judges, not a stated binary refusal rate. The paper also reports attack-method comparisons and ablations; only results that directly report attack outcomes are included.
record.test_reason: The paper reports graded harmful-compliance rates when optimized adversarial suffixes (GCG, Faster-GCG) target a 'Sure, here is' opening. It covers five open aligned models, two benchmarks, transfer to three proprietary models, three defenses and a reasoning mode. This bears on the suffix part of V4 in new models and settings. It is mainly an attack-efficiency paper: it reports no no-attack baseline, and its 'baselines' are other attack methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Faster-GCG gives about 8× better sample efficiency and higher ASR than GCG across models and datasets. They add that jailbreaks remain a persistent vulnerability requiring more robust alignment. Their statement on defenses is that ASRs drop but Faster-GCG still beats GCG.
record.recipe_differences: This study optimizes adversarial suffixes with gradient-based discrete search and evaluates harmfulness. It does not fine-tune models or measure response-position KL as in the claim's linked mechanisms.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with model, dataset, suffix length and placement, batch size, defense, transfer target, and reasoning versus non-reasoning mode. The paper reports that ASRs are lower with defenses and in reasoning mode; Faster-GCG++ changes suffix length and placement.
record.problems: ASR is described as an average of normalized scores from two judges, rather than a binary refusal rate. No uncertainty estimates for the reported ASRs are stated. Transfer, defense, and reasoning results are reported under distinct settings, and some transfer ASRs are low.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other attack-method ASRs in Tables 1 and A2 (including AutoDAN, I-GCG, GCG-PS, TAO, and black-box methods), Faster-I-GCG results, the Table 4 component ablations, Table 5 hyperparameter sweep, and Table 2 batch-size-64 entries duplicated by Table 1. These were left out to prioritize the core GCG/Faster-GCG suffix outcomes across datasets, models, transfer, defenses, and reasoning conditions.

untested.parts: All: no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling a compliant start (explicitly excluded by the threat model) and decoding changes. No no-attack refusal baseline is reported.
All: no analysis of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: Other GCG-family suffix attacks (I-GCG, GCG-PS, TAO, Faster-I-GCG) are suffix bypass results on the same models; I-GCG reaches 89.6% and Faster-I-GCG 91.7% on Llama2-7B.
No no-attack baseline (harmfulness of plain harmful prompts) is reported, so bypass size relative to baseline refusal cannot be computed.

record.verdict_notes: ASR is a graded harmfulness score: the mean of two LLM judges (GPT-4-Judge style via GPT-oss-20B, and StrongREJECT via Llama-3.1-8B), taking the best of the top-10 suffixes per example. It is not a binary refusal rate. Rows comparing Faster-GCG with GCG are method comparisons; the GCG 'baseline' is another attack, not a control. Faster-GCG++ prepends the adversarial tokens rather than appending them. The reader's 'challenges' label for GPT-5-mini was folded into limits_scope because the suffixes were transferred, not optimized on that target.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling compliant response tokens and decoding changes are not tested. The study tests optimized adversarial suffix attacks, including suffix placement before or after the prompt.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens, and robustness of such training.

relationships.condition: White-box suffixes optimized toward a 'Sure, here is' target on open models (Llama2-7B, Qwen3-4B, Gemma3-4B, Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3.5-4B), JBB and AdvBench, non-reasoning mode
relationships.reason: Graded harmfulness ASR is 46–89% across models and datasets for GCG, Faster-GCG and Faster-GCG++, e.g. jbb-gcg-g3 80.6%, jbb-plus-q35 88.7%, adv-plus-q3 83.9%.
relationships.display_finding: Graded harmfulness attack success was 46–89% across models and datasets for GCG, Faster-GCG and Faster-GCG++, with the strongest runs at 80.6–88.7%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: White-box suffixes optimized toward a 'Sure, here is' target on open models (Llama2-7B, Qwen3-4B, Gemma3-4B, Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3.5-4B), JBB and AdvBench, non-reasoning mode
source_check.reason: Tables 1 and 3 show substantial model- and method-dependent incompleteness, including 45.9–54.2% scores, alongside stronger results. Under the mixed-results rule, this broad condition requires qualification; supports can be retained for narrower high-scoring groups.

relationships.condition: Qwen3.5-4B in reasoning mode, with the target moved to after </think>
relationships.reason: ASR falls from 77.9–88.7% in non-reasoning mode (reason-nr-*) to 30.5–37.4% in reasoning mode (reason-r-gcg, reason-r-fast, reason-r-plus).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success fell from 77.9–88.7% in non-reasoning mode to 30.5–37.4% in reasoning mode.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Qwen3.5-4B in reasoning mode, with the target moved to after </think>
source_check.reason: Table A5 gives reasoning-mode scores of 30.5%, 32.6% and 37.4%, compared with 77.9%, 78.7% and 88.7% without reasoning; Appendix G.4 specifies the modified target.

relationships.condition: Suffixes transferred from Qwen3.5 to proprietary models
relationships.reason: Transfer ASR is 0.0–5.6% on Gemini-3-flash and GPT-5-mini and 16–21.5% on Sonnet-4 (transfer-* rows), so the bypass largely needs white-box optimization on the target.
relationships.display_finding: Transferred suffixes reached 0.0–5.6% on Gemini-3-flash and GPT-5-mini and 16–21.5% on Sonnet-4, so the bypass largely needs white-box optimization on the target.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Suffixes transferred from Qwen3.5 to proprietary models
source_check.reason: Table A3 gives 4.1–5.6% on Gemini, 0.0–0.6% on GPT-5-mini and 16.0–21.5% on Sonnet-4. These results establish limited transfer for the tested surrogate and attacks; they do not establish that target-specific white-box optimization is generally necessary.

relationships.condition: Llama2-7B with prompt-level defenses (PPL filter, Self-reminder, RPO)
relationships.reason: ASR drops from 58–66% undefended to 9.6–34.2% (def-* rows); the authors note adaptive attacks might recover it.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success dropped from 58–66% undefended to 9.6–34.2% under these defenses; the authors note that adaptive attacks might recover it.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 19 May 2026; its experiments should not be dated solely by the record's 2024 year. ASR is graded harmfulness, with the best score selected among ten lowest-loss candidates per example; it is not a binary compliance fraction.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Optimized suffix attacks on JBB-Behaviors and AdvBench open-source models
reader_labels.reason: The reported attack scores show harmful outputs across models and datasets, including high scores in several conditions; see jbb-gcg-g3, jbb-fast-g3, jbb-plus-q35, adv-plus-q3, and adv-plus-q35, among others.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Transfer to proprietary models, defended settings, and reasoning mode
reader_labels.reason: Transfer ASRs are low in some targets, defenses substantially reduce scores, and reasoning-mode results are lower than non-reasoning results; see transfer-gem-gcg through transfer-sonnet-fast, def-ppl-gcg through def-rpo-fast, and reason-r-gcg through reason-r-plus.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported GCG transfer ASR is 0.0%, so this attack did not produce the predicted bypass in this target condition; see transfer-gpt-gcg.
